research_question: Does increased triadic functional connectivity in region-set X correlate with sustained attention scores?
falsifiability_criteria: If the correlation between triadic connectivity and sustained attention scores is not significant after multiplicity correction (p >= 0.05, FDR-corrected), the hypothesis is falsified.
primary_endpoint: Pearson correlation between triadic connectivity index and sustained attention task score
secondary_endpoints: pairwise functional connectivity as a comparison baseline
alternative_explanations: head motion artifact could inflate connectivity estimates
practice effects on the attention task across sessions

sources.title: High-Order Triadic Functional Connectivity in the Brain and Beyond

condition_label_definitions.rest: eyes-closed resting state, no task instructions
condition_label_definitions.task: sustained attention task with visual targets

null_model.description: Fourier phase randomization preserving power spectrum, 1000 surrogates

leakage_controls: subject-level train/test split enforced before any preprocessing
known_leakage_risks: repeated sessions from the same subject could leak subject identity across folds
measurement_limitations: fMRI temporal resolution limits detection of fast triadic dynamics
claim_language: We hypothesize an association between triadic connectivity and sustained attention; this is a correlational, exploratory analysis.
replication_plan: Pre-register and replicate on an independent held-out cohort (ds006644) before any confirmatory claim.
